name.value: Length Tally of the Handing Order

description.value: A flat shell plate carrying the numbers of forty-two weir lengths in their handing order, cut as notches along both edges and read from the seaward end inward. It was made in 2244 at the survey's request by a household which then declined to keep it, on the ground that a record of the order outlasting a term is a claim about a term that has not happened. The plate is complete and uncracked and the twine loop is a modern replacement. It remains the only representation of the order in existence, and the households consider it inaccurate in principle rather than in detail.

notes.value: Accessioned as a gift and catalogued as a commission, which are different things in the ethics register and were the same afternoon on the flats.
